assessment: The incumbent delivers a removable, assembled partition set and includes an order check and layout diagram. These provide plausible opportunities to catch selection and placement errors, but their effectiveness is unmeasured. Reported component errors and unpacking confusion indicate distinct possible failures; neither establishes their cause. O6 limits an account of uniformly slow assembly: both workers achieved seven to nine minutes on repeated three-compartment orders, whereas mixed batches contained every extreme delay. Layout complexity and switching remain confounded. O5 also weakens a width-only explanation for insertion retries because measured widths overlap. The combined timing cannot identify the dominant delay. Current evidence does not demonstrate any pilot success threshold.

openings.claim: Repeated changes between order layouts may increase selection and checking work, contributing to mixed-batch delays and component errors.
openings.delta: Tests whether order switching contributes beyond the inherent work of larger layouts.
openings.prediction: For the same layouts and worker, mixed sequences increase selection/checking time or discrepancies relative to grouped sequences, without a comparable increase in insertion time.
openings.probe: Reuse six spare sample organizers across grouped and mixed sequences containing identical layout counts; reverse sequence order between workers. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, and audit components against each order. Treat practice and reuse effects as limitations. Stop the probe before it threatens accepted-order delivery.
assumptions: Sample trials fit available working time and the initial spending cap.
Reusable sample cycles approximate production sufficiently for an exploratory comparison.

openings.claim: An order-specific diagram explicitly locating the short partition may improve unaided arrangement with the existing removable parts.
openings.delta: Tests layout interpretation after independently verifying component completeness.
openings.prediction: Verified complete kits with the tailored diagram produce fewer short-partition placement questions than equivalent kits with the current diagram.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten participants, five per diagram, using the same ordered layout and verified parts. Record unaided completion and short-partition questions within ten minutes. This is an exploratory discriminator, not proof of 90% success. Check printing cost and preparation time before production use.
assumptions: Diagram preparation fits the fixed delivery date and 500 initial/0.40 recurring cost limits.
Instructions alone can resolve at least some observed placement confusion.
